Seasonal forecast skill for Layer A

Can a pre-season forecast pick out bad long-rains seasons at the Nakuru pilot wards well enough to pay a seed voucher before planting? Measured against our CHIRPS ward rainfall, 1981–2016 for the C3S hindcasts and 1998 onward for GHACOF.

Research, not product terms. Ward locations are placeholders; prices use the illustrative loadings and voucher value. Verification is leave-one-out: a season's own rainfall never sets the tercile boundary it is judged by.

Answers

Long rains (March–May), C3S SEAS5.1: correlation 0.33 (95% interval 0.00 to 0.59), ROC area 0.65. Against the rule set before the analysis (correlation 95% interval above zero AND ROC area for below-normal >= 0.6) it passes, only at the margin. Neighbouring 1-degree cells give correlations of 0.37, 0.34, 0.35, 0.22.
Short rains (October–December), C3S SEAS5.1: correlation 0.54 (95% interval 0.26 to 0.74), ROC area 0.69: clearly skilful, as the literature says.
Layer A re-priced with measured skill (0.33 instead of the 0.45 placeholder): vouchers in 17% of seasons, expected cost KES 340 and gross KES 754 per acre, catching 25% of Layer B payout seasons. Run directly on the C3S hindcast, the 45% trigger fired in 6 of 36 seasons and caught 18% of Layer B payout seasons.
Early-season trigger (EXPERIMENTAL): at day 35 after planting, Ward A's projected WRSI correlates 0.58 with the final WRSI (0.35 without the CHIRPS-GEFS forecast). It fires in 0% of seasons 2000–2025 and catches 0% of seasons that end below the trigger; a 20% early payout costs KES 0 gross per acre.
Short-rains pilot candidates in semi-arid eastern Kenya: 1362 of 3000 CHIRPS cells have OND wetter than MAM and at least 250 mm in 60% of OND seasons, mostly near Mbooni, Kitui, Mwingi. Report only; nothing added to the pilot.
IRI archived USGS WRSI: iridl.ldeo.columbia.edu/SOURCES/.USGS/.ADDS/ redirects to the sign-in page, so browsing it needs a (free) account. IRI's data-download URLs work without one, which is how the C3S hindcasts here were fetched.

(a) Published evidence

As given in the brief (not re-derived here): Walker et al. (2019) find near-zero GloSea skill for the East African long rains (r = 0.07) and much higher skill for the short rains (r = 0.69); GHACOF consensus skill is low except some skill in the below-normal category over Kenya. Our measurements use a different model (ECMWF SEAS5.1 through C3S), a single 1-degree cell and 36 seasons, so a higher long-rains value here is within sampling noise of "low" and should not be read as contradicting it.

(d) Early-season trigger EXPERIMENTAL

About 35 days after the start of season, project the end-of-season WRSI from observed rain to date, the CHIRPS-GEFS 15-day forecast issued that day, and leave-one-out climatology for the rest; pay 20% of sum insured if the projection is below the WRSI trigger (80). Priced separately; not in the product.

As specified, the trigger compares the projection with the WRSI trigger itself. By day 35 only about a quarter of the season has been observed, and climatology fills in the rest, so projections cluster near normal: the lowest projection at Ward A was 82. For information only, here is how a higher projection threshold would score against seasons that actually ended below 80:

At Ward B the projection is the same with or without the forecast: its deep (placeholder) soil absorbs any 15-day difference, so the crop is rarely short of water either way. One CHIRPS-GEFS file needed (2020, day 96) is missing on the CHC server (HTTP 404), so 2020 is excluded.
